study_id: Miller et al. - 2019 - Predictive Abilities of Machine Learning Techniques May Be Limited by Dataset Characteristics Insig

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study analyzes adult heart transplant recipients using non-linear machine learning models (e.g., neural networks, random forest) to predict 1‑year survival, meeting all population, intervention, comparator, outcome, and study design criteria.

identification_methods.Setting: Analysis of UNOS national registry data
identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective analysis comparing machine learning and traditional statistical models for 1‑year survival after heart transplantation.
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Adult patients ≥18 years undergoing first single‑organ heart transplantation; excluded >20% missing data.
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: Neural networks, naive Bayes, tree‑augmented naive Bayes, support vector machines, random forest, stochastic gradient boosting (plus logistic regression, ridge regression, LASSO for comparison)
identification_methods.Comparator: Traditional statistical methods (logistic regression, ridge regression, LASSO)
identification_methods.Input Variables: Donor and recipient age, creatinine, body mass index, liver function tests, aspartate transaminase, hemodynamics, donor blood pH, candidate diagnosis, etc.
identification_methods.Missing Data Handling: Patients with >20% missing data were excluded; no imputation performed.
identification_methods.Validation Method: 80% training / 20% testing split; serial bootstrapping (10 repetitions); cross‑validation reported.
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Calibration curves, Hosmer‑Lemeshow test, Brier scores used; analyses performed in R 3.2.2.

population.Inclusion criteria: Adult patients (≥18 years) undergoing their first single-organ heart transplantation
population.Population Notes: Data split into 80% training and 20% testing sets; analyses performed across three time periods and UNOS regions

interventions_outcomes.Specific Algorithm Name: neural networks, naive-Bayes, tree-augmented naive-Bayes, support vector machines, random forest, stochastic gradient boosting
interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: UNOS clinical registry data (demographic and clinical variables)
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Models trained on 80% of data, tested on remaining 20%; bootstrapping applied 10 times; calibration assessed with Hosmer-Lemeshow and Brier scores
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Primary outcome was 1-year mortality/survival after heart transplantation
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: All models showed modest discrimination with C-statistics around 0.65-0.66; neural network highest at 0.66
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reported against: Traditional statistical models (logistic regression, ridge regression, LASSO)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: Adult heart transplant recipients in UNOS database
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reporting: C-statistic 0.66 for neural network, 0.65 for traditional models
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: Area under the ROC curve (AUC) calculated on held-out test set
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: Modest discrimination; machine learning did not improve prediction over traditional models
